'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**Four [[Chadian soldier]]s are killed and many more are wounded when their base is attacked by [[jihadism|jihadists]] in [[Aguelhok]], [[Kidal Region|Kidal]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/2/four-peacekeepers-killed-in-northern-mali-attack-un (Al Jazeera)]
*[[United States Capitol car attack]]
**A [[United States Capitol Police|Capitol Police]] officer is killed and another is wounded after [[vehicle-ramming attack|being struck by a vehicle]] outside [[Capitol Hill]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] The attacker is shot dead after lunging at the officers with a knife. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-56620113 (BBC News)]
*[[Far-right terrorism in Spain]]
**The regional office of the [[Left-wing politics|leftist]] [[Unidas Podemos]] party in [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]], [[Region of Murcia|Murcia]], is [[Arson|firebomb]]ed, leaving damage to its exterior. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spain-politics-attack/fire-bomb-attack-on-spanish-leftist-partys-office-idUSKBN2BP0RD (Reuters)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**At least four civilians were injured in anti-Indian protests against the killing of three suspected rebels by [[Indian Army|Indian soldiers]] in [[Kashmir]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/2/anti-india-clashes-erupt-after-troops-kill-three-kashmir-rebels#:~:text=At%20least%20four%20civilians%20were,soldiers%20in%20Indian%2Dadministered%20Kashmir. (Al Jazeera0]

'''Arts and culture'''
*A sealed copy of the 1985 [[Nintendo Entertainment System]] game ''[[Super Mario Bros.]]'' sells at auction for [[United States dollar|US$]]660,000, the most ever paid for a single video game. [https://www.ksl.com/article/50139553/rare-super-mario-bros-game-sells-for-a-record-660000 (KSL-TV)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Aftermath of the [[Battle of Palma]]
**French energy company [[Total SE]] ceases operations and [[emergency evacuation|evacuates]] all of its staff from its [[Gas-fired power plant|power plant]] in the [[Cabo Delgado Province]], after [[Islamic State's Central Africa Province|IS-CAP]] [[insurgent]]s infiltrate a security perimeter surrounding the [[liquefied natural gas]] reserves where the plant is located. [https://www.trtworld.com/africa/france-s-total-reportedly-evacuates-staff-shuts-gas-site-in-mozambique-45556 (TRT World)]
*Canadian airlines [[Air Canada]] and [[Air Transat]] mutually terminate a planned [[Mergers and acquisitions|merger]] deal after failing to secure an approval from the [[European Commission]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/air-canada-transat-merger-1.5974439 (CBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Hualien train derailment]]
**At least 50 people are killed and 156 others are wounded when a [[Taroko Express]] train, headed for the celebration of the [[Qingming Festival|Tomb Sweeping festival]], [[derailment|derails]] in [[Hualien County|Hualien]], [[Taiwan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56612248 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[India]] reports a new single-day record of 3.67 million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] administered. [https://www.livemint.com/news/india/india-records-highest-ever-single-day-covid-19-vaccinations-11617348039782.html (Livemint)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****[[Maharashtra]] reports a record 47,827 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://m.timesofindia.com/india/maharashtra-reports-record-47827-covid-cases-mumbai-sees-highest-daily-spike/amp_articleshow/81875673.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 6,830 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 624,594. The country also reports its highest ever seven-day moving average of deaths with 50. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/04/02/covid-19-bangladesh-records-50-more-deaths-6-830-new-cases-in-24hrs (Dhaka Tribune)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]]
****Mohammed Oreibi al-Khalifa, a former [[Iraq]] judge who presided during the [[Trial of Saddam Hussein|trial]] of former dictator [[Saddam Hussein]], dies from COVID-19 at the age of 52. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/04/02/Coronavirus-Iraq-judge-who-presided-over-Saddam-Hussein-s-trial-dies-of-COVID-19 (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports a record 15,310 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which includes 3,709 cases that were not reported since March 31. This brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 771,497. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/04/02/21/highest-ever-philippines-reports-15310-covid-19-cases-37k-from-backlogs (ABS-CBN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bosnia and Herzegovina]]
****[[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] reports a record 2,154 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the first time that daily cases surpassed 2,000 in the country. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/bosnia_records_highest_daily_number_of_covid_19_cases-2118389/ (''The National Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] suspends the administration of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[vaccine]] to people under 60 years old following the death of a woman who had received the vaccine. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/astrazeneca-vaccine-netherlands-europe-b1826127.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 42,308 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.4 million. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkeys-covid-19-cases-continue-to-hit-record-high/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 19,893 new confirmed cases and 433 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.71 million and the nationwide death toll to 33,679. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-infection-hits-new-records-with-19893-cases-433-deaths.html?cn-reloaded=1 (''Kyiv Post'')]

***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] reports that over 100 million people have received their [[Priming (immunology)|first dose]] of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://www.businessinsider.com/over-100-million-people-in-us-first-dose-covid-19-vaccine-2021-4 (''Business Insider'')] [https://www.forbes.com/sites/joewalsh/2021/04/02/us-just-vaccinated-over-100-million-americans/?sh=319293604b8f (''Forbes'')]

***[[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.thecourier.com.au/story/7194705/argentinian-president-positive-for-covid/?cs=10230 (''The Courier'')]

'''International relations'''
*The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] lifts sanctions that targeted several members of the [[International Criminal Court]], such as [[Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court|Chief Prosecutor]] [[Fatou Bensouda]] and human rights lawyer [[Phakiso Mochochoko]]. They were sanctioned last year by former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] for investigating allegations of war crimes committed [[International Criminal Court investigation in Afghanistan|in Afghanistan]] and the [[Palestinian territories]]. The administration maintains that the ICC lacked jurisdiction in both cases, as neither the U.S. nor Israel are member states. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/2/us-lifts-trumps-sanctions-on-icc-prosecutor-court-official (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Northern Ireland riots]]
**Eight [[Police Service of Northern Ireland|police]] officers are injured and eight people are arrested during a [[riot]] in [[Sandy Row]], south [[Belfast]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/apr/03/northern-ireland-secretary-calls-for-calm-after-belfast-riots (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Far-right terrorism in the United Kingdom]], [[History of the Metropolitan Police]]
**22-year-old [[Metropolitan Police]] [[Constable]] Ben Hannam admits to possession of an [[child pornography|indecent image of a child]], and a judge accordingly lifts reporting restrictions designed to allow a [[fair trial]], revealing that Hannam became the first serving UK officer to be convicted of a [[Terrorism Acts|terror offence]] after being found guilty at the [[Old Bailey]] of [[National Action (UK)|National Action]] membership. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/apr/01/ben-hannam-met-police-officer-guilty-belonging-banned-neo-nazi-terror-group (''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Major League Baseball All-Star Game]]
**[[Major League Baseball]] announces that it will move this year's [[MLB All-Star Game|All-Star Game]] from [[Atlanta]] in response to the [[U.S. state]] of [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] passing a [[Republican efforts to make voting laws more restrictive following the 2020 presidential election#Georgia|series of controversial voting laws]] that critics say disproportionately target the state's minority voters. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/2021/04/02/mlb-all-star-game-atlanta-moved-georgia-voting-law/7066061002/ (''USA Today'')]
